prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name a single universal “best” roofer for Denver (that depends on your location, roof type and budget), but I can help you find the right, reputable contractor and give you a short list of things to check so you don’t get stuck with a storm‑chaser or low‑quality work.

If you want, I can look up top rated local roofers for your exact area—tell me your Denver zip code and whether you want only roofers that work with insurance claims.

Quick checklist to find the best roofer for hail damage in Denver
- Experience with hail/storm claims and working with insurers (ask how they handle the adjuster and Xactimate estimates).  
- Certifications from major shingle manufacturers (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred, etc.).  
- Current insurance: general liability and workers’ comp. Ask for certificates.  
- Local permanent business address and long track record (not a one‑truck storm chaser).  
- Written, itemized estimate and clear scope (materials, layers removed, decking repair, flashing, vents).  
- Written warranties: workmanship plus manufacturer’s shingle warranty. Get both in writing.  
- Will pull permits and arrange inspections if required by the city or county.  
- Good reviews on Google/Yelp/Angi and an A or good rating with the BBB. Ask for recent local references.  
- Reasonable deposit (often 10–30%); be cautious about very large upfront payments. Don’t sign an assignment of benefits unless you understand it.  

Questions to ask a roofer before hiring
- How many hail jobs have you completed in the past year in Denver?  
- Are you a certified installer for the shingle brand you recommend? Can you show certificates?  
- Will you provide an itemized estimate and coordinate/meet with my insurance adjuster?  
- Do you pull permits and provide post‑job inspection documentation?  
- What are your labor and manufacturer warranty terms?  

Where to search and verify
- Google and Yelp reviews (read several recent reviews).  
- Angi/HomeAdvisor for pre‑screened pros.  
- Better Business Bureau for complaints/resolution history.  
- Manufacturer locators (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed) to find certified contractors.  

Red flags
- Door‑to‑door sales immediately after a storm claiming “this will fail soon” pressure tactics.  
- Contractor asks you to sign assignment of benefits right away.  
- No written estimate, no permit pull, or demands for very large upfront cash payments.  
- Vague warranty promises or inability to show insurance certificates.

If you give me your zip code (or neighborhood) I’ll pull together a short list of highly‑rated Denver roofers that specialize in hail damage and work with insurance, plus contact tips and sample questions tailored to each one.
